section_1.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
section_1.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in 2D space with magnitude and direction. Introduce scalar multiplication (stretching) and vector addition (the parallelogram rule) as the fundamental building blocks.
section_1.example: Visualizing a drone moving 2 units East and 3 units North as a vector (2,3).

section_2.title: Linear Combinations and Span
section_2.content: Explain that a linear combination is the sum of scaled vectors. Define 'Span' as the set of all possible points reachable by scaling and adding a set of vectors. Use an animation showing the tip of the vector moving across the plane.
section_2.example: Using two vectors v1=(1,0) and v2=(0,1), show that every point (x,y) in 2D space can be reached, meaning the span is the entire 2D plane.

section_3.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule
section_3.content: Explain that linear dependence occurs when at least one vector in a set is 'redundant'—it can be formed by a combination of the others. Visually show a third vector lying on the line formed by two others, adding no new 'reach'.
section_3.example: Two robots moving; if Robot B just follows Robot A's path exactly, Robot B adds no new capability to the system.

section_4.title: Defining the Basis
section_4.content: Define a 'Basis' as the minimal set of vectors that spans the entire space without any redundancy (linearly independent). Emphasize that a basis is the 'efficient coordinate system' for a space.
section_4.example: Comparing a 2D map using 3 vectors (redundant) versus 2 vectors (a basis); the basis is the 'perfect' set of directions to describe any location.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Review the progression: Linear combinations build a span; if the span is redundant, it's linearly dependent; remove the redundancy, and you find the basis. Connect this to the concept of 'dimension'.
section_5.example: Visualizing a 3D coordinate system (x, y, z) as the 'basis' for a digital 3D game environment.
